CHIEF COMPLAINT
Followup of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Bruce is a 60-year-old male with a past medical history significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension who presents for followup of his chronic problems. Patient reports it has been a crazy year and a half with anxiety and pressure related to holiday preparations that has been wearing on him. He did have a nice holiday and was glad to see family after about two years, though it was a lot of work and stressful. He is planning to take a vacation somewhere nice and warm.

Regarding depression, patient tried new strategies over the summer, starting long walks outside every morning when the weather was nice and the plants were in full bloom. This encouraged him to do yard work on weekends, which was a nice way to be active and get sun. However, with the seasons changing and getting cold, he has not been able to continue this and needs to find something new. He is not ready to try medications and would like to look into alternative options. He denies any thoughts of harming himself or others.

Regarding diabetes, patient reports getting through Halloween okay but did not stick to diet much during Thanksgiving week, though it is improving. He has been trying to monitor his sugar intake. He is still taking metformin.

Regarding hypertension, patient reports purchasing the blood pressure cuff as recommended. Readings have been pretty moderate with nothing out of the ordinary. He is still taking lisinopril with no problems.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, belly pain, blood in stool, or weight loss.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, type 2 diabetes, hypertension.

MEDICATIONS
Metformin, lisinopril.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient enjoys outdoor activities including walking and yard work. He is planning a vacation. Seasonal changes have affected his ability to maintain outdoor activity routine.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure looks good. Neck: No carotid bruits appreciated. Heart: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base, consistent with past findings and not clinically significant. Lungs: Clear. Lower extremities: 1+ non-pitting edema bilaterally.

RESULTS
EKG: No evidence of concern, everything looks good. Hemoglobin A1C: 8 (elevated, goal closer to 6).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Depression: Refer to psychiatry for talk therapy. Type 2 diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1C in the next couple months, increase metformin to 1000 mg twice daily, and order lipid panel. Hypertension: Order echocardiogram to recheck heart murmur and continue lisinopril 20 mg daily.
